title: PM Modi Hails Indian-American Community's Role as India Marks Independence Day
excerpt: While Modi praised the diaspora's contributions, the muted response from senior US officials beyond FBI Director Kash Patel and Secretary of State Marco Rubio signaled underlying strains in bilateral ties.
body:
• Prime Minister Modi hailed the Indian-American community's contributions during India's Independence Day celebrations, calling diaspora members ambassadors of Indian values.
  • FBI Director Kash Patel and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were the only senior US officials to extend greetings — a notably muted response compared to previous administrations.
  • India's Ambassador to the US, Vinay Kwatra, praised the diaspora's role in strengthening bilateral ties at community celebrations.
  • The subdued engagement from Washington is seen as reflecting current strains in the India-US relationship under the Trump administration.

Modi Praises Diaspora as 'Ambassadors of Indian Values'

As India celebrated its Independence Day on August 15, Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the nation from the Red Fort in New Delhi and took the occasion to recognize the Indian-American community's role in bridging ties between the two countries. Modi praised members of the diaspora as ambassadors who carry Indian values wherever they go, a theme he has consistently emphasized in his outreach to the estimated 4.8 million Indian Americans, according to India Tribune.

The Prime Minister's Red Fort addresses have now cumulatively clocked a record 1,177 minutes across his tenure — surpassing the combined totals of Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi, and Manmohan Singh, India Tribune reported.

Muted Greetings From Washington

While Modi spoke warmly of the diaspora, the diplomatic signals from Washington told a more complicated story. FBI Director Kash Patel and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were the only senior American officials to extend Independence Day greetings to India, IndiaWest reported — a notably low-key engagement compared to previous administrations when India's national day typically drew broader recognition from the White House and State Department.

Patel, whose parents hail from Gujarat and migrated to the US from Canada after fleeing ethnic repression in Uganda, shared his wishes on social media, highlighting Modi's Red Fort address. Rubio described the US-India relationship as "consequential and far-reaching," noting cooperation in industries, technology, innovation, and space.

"The two democracies are working together to tackle modern challenges and ensure a brighter future for both nations."

— Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Independence Day statement

The absence of greetings from the president or vice president stands in contrast with Biden-era engagement, when India's Independence Day regularly received recognition from the highest levels of the US government. Observers see this as a subtle reflection of current bilateral strains.

Community Celebrations Across the US

Indian-American communities marked the occasion with events across major metropolitan areas. India's Ambassador to the United States, Vinay Kwatra, praised the diaspora's role in strengthening US-India ties at community gatherings, according to India Tribune.

In the Chicago area, the Federation of Indian Associations organized celebrations that drew hundreds of attendees. The Bay Area saw its annual FOG India Day Parade in Fremont on August 16, featuring cultural showcases, food, and community activities. Similar events took place across New York, Houston, Dallas, and other cities with significant Indian-American populations.

A Relationship Under Pressure

The muted diplomatic engagement comes during a period of tensions between Washington and New Delhi on multiple fronts. Trade disagreements, differing positions on geopolitical flashpoints, and immigration policy friction have all complicated the bilateral relationship in recent months.

Modi and Trump last met on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in France, where they discussed cooperation across trade, technology, defense, and people-to-people exchanges. On July 4, Modi had extended warm wishes to Trump on the United States' 250th Independence Day, describing the India-US friendship as "a force for global good."

For Indian Americans navigating their identity between two countries, the diplomatic temperature matters. The community has historically served as a bridge between the world's two largest democracies — a role that both governments acknowledge even when official relations hit turbulence.
